headline: RFQs still take days to quote?
symptoms: Every RFQ waits for one person to read the drawing

seo.title: CNC RFQ Quoting Software for Machine Shops | deltaV
seo.description: RFQ quoting for CNC and job shops: reads each drawing, flags cost drivers, suggests hours from similar past jobs and turns won quotes into travelers.

workflow.heading: CNC quoting software around your shop
workflow.intro: The prototype uses sample jobs. For your shop, we'd map the path from an RFQ to an approved quote and job record, using the drawing requirements and estimating rules your team works with.
steps: Keep the drawing revision, material, quantity and requested delivery together. Missing details go back for clarification.
Compare similar jobs and actual hours. The estimator checks setup, machining, outside work and uncertain tolerances before approving a price.
Agree which fields reach your ERP, traveler and inspection plan. Keep the accepted revision attached to the job.
Use recorded setup and run hours to see where an estimate differed. Sparse history stays visible rather than becoming a confident guess.
review: An RFQ you can share, your estimating sheet and where actual hours are recorded. We'd check available history, approval rules and the connection to the tools you keep.

faq: Does it price jobs without the estimator?
No. It drafts the estimate; the estimator approves every price.
Can it work alongside Paperless Parts or our ERP?
We'd check the available API or exports and agree the field mapping before building the connection. The aim is to fill gaps around the tools you keep, such as RFQ intake and quote-vs-actual.
Where do the suggested hours come from?
The proposed workflow uses your own quote and actual-hours history. When that history is sparse, the estimator reviews the assumptions.
What happens when a drawing is incomplete?
The workflow should flag missing material, revision or requirements for review. An estimator resolves them before the quote is approved.
